original:
H2: CData Connect AI lets you plug any business application into any AI tool — like Salesforce into Anthropic Claude — for live, trusted answers and actions with zero data copies.
H3: Give Salesforce rich semantic context and real-time data from Anthropic Claude so it can answer precisely and take safe, effective actions across your business.
experiment:
H2: CData Connect AI lets you plug any business application into any AI tool — like Salesforce into Anthropic Claude
remove H3 --> move CTAs up
- Instant answers, from live [datasource] data — and any other source in one prompt
- Reliable queries on day one — no schema setup, no field-name guesswork
- Automate [datasource] workflows safely — [llm] acts within your access rules
hypothesis: By trimming down the text-heavy block in the hero, highlighting the CTAs, and adding more readily grasped bullet points consistently about the benefits of Connect AI, the CTR of the CTAs shall rise.
title: Benefit bullets
evaluation: No usable baseline: the measurement history starts with this experiment, so no clean pre-period exists. The period itself established the reference level for this page type — 11.6% paid trial-intent CTR, measured on a solid base of ~210 paid sessions/day with normal day-to-day variation — that later experiments are measured against.
suggestions: Keep a stable 1–2 week measurement window before any first-of-its-kind change so a weekday-aligned baseline exists. Benefit-focused phrasing can be re-tested later against the feature-bullet benchmark.

original:
H2: CData Connect AI lets you plug any business application into any AI tool — like Salesforce into Anthropic Claude — for live, trusted answers and actions with zero data copies.
H3: Give Salesforce rich semantic context and real-time data from Anthropic Claude so it can answer precisely and take safe, effective actions across your business.
experiment:
H2: CData Connect AI lets you plug any business application into any AI tool — like Salesforce into Anthropic Claude — like Salesforce into Anthropic Claude — for live, trusted answers and actions with zero data copies.
remove H3 --> move CTAs up
- Schema-aware MCP server — [ai-agent] reads your full [datasource] data model on connect
- Cross-source MCP toolset — join live [datasource] with hundreds of other systems in one prompt
- Bidirectional with identity passthrough — [ai-agent] reads and writes under your access rules
hypothesis: By trimming down the text-heavy block in the hero, highlighting the CTAs, and adding more readily grasped bullet points consistently about the features of Connect AI, the CTR of the CTAs shall rise.
title: Feature bullets
evaluation: Clear winner: feature-focused bullets lifted the paid trial-intent CTR from 11.6% to 15.0% (+29%) versus the preceding benefit-focused version. The audience on these datasource pages — technical evaluators — responds better to concrete capabilities than to outcome promises. Traffic note: the paid base more than halved between the two windows (~210 → ~94 sessions/day), so the comparison rests on unequal volumes; a lift of this size is unlikely to be a volume artifact alone, but the exact magnitude carries some uncertainty.
suggestions: Test phrasing variants within the feature direction: concrete numbers ("300+ sources") vs. generic ("hundreds"), and the order of the three bullets. Try one hybrid bullet (feature + one-line benefit) against pure features.

original: H2: Connect your AI assistants and agents to hundreds of enterprise systems in minutes with a managed Model Context Protocol (MCP) platform
experiment:
The page shall display all 11 supported AI agents above the fold, each linking to the general Connect AI sign-up page.
The H2 shall be the headline for the AI agent logos
The general CTA moves up.
hypothesis: By recognizing that this page is about connecting business data to their desired AI agent, the users should be encouraged to click on its logo and start a Connect AI trial.
title: Agent logo grid
evaluation: Negative: presenting all 11 agent logos above the fold cut the organic trial-intent CTR from 24.5% to 19.3% (−21%). The clicks the logos collected did not offset the weakened primary CTA — eleven equally weighted choices diluted attention rather than helping visitors self-select. The traffic base was stable across both windows (~63 vs. ~58 organic sessions/day), making this one of the cleaner comparisons in the series.
suggestions: If agent logos return above the fold, test a curated set of 3 with one visually dominant "recommended" agent. Order logos by the visitor's likely intent (e.g. paid landing keyword or referrer).

original:

H3: Give Salesforce rich semantic context and real-time data from Anthropic Claude so it can answer precisely and take safe, effective actions across your business.
experiment:
H2: CData Connect AI lets you plug any business application into any AI tool — like Salesforce into Anthropic Claude — like Salesforce into Anthropic Claude — for live, trusted answers and actions with zero data copies.
remove H3 --> move CTAs up
- One MCP server, hundreds of live sources — [llm] reaches [datasource] and any other system through a single managed connection, no per-source setup
- Schema-aware from the first prompt — [llm] reads your full [datasource] data model on connect, so answers are accurate on day one
- Bidirectional and secure by design — [llm] reads and writes live [datasource] data within your own access rules
hypothesis: By trimming down the text-heavy block in the hero, highlighting the CTAs, and adding more readily grasped bullet points consistently about the value proposition of Connect AI, the CTR of the CTAs shall rise.
title: Value bullets
evaluation: Mild negative: value-proposition phrasing underperformed the feature bullets it replaced (15.0% → 13.6%, −9%). Caveat: the pattern's paid volume jumped +80% during this window (~94 → ~169 sessions/day, with daily swings of ±50%), driven by a large non-converting Japanese paid-traffic wave on the salesforce-to-claude page — the pure copy effect is likely smaller than the raw number, though the direction (features > value-prop) matches the surrounding tests.
suggestions: Treat feature-focused copy as the control going forward. Spend the next test slot on non-copy levers (visuals, CTA styling, social proof) rather than another abstraction-level copy variant.

original: H2: Connect your AI assistants and agents to hundreds of enterprise systems in minutes with a managed Model Context Protocol (MCP) platform
experiment:
roll back to the previous version:
- remove AI agent icons
- remove AI agent icons
- use the AI agent icon headline as H2 between H1 and CTA again:
Connect your AI assistants and agents to hundreds of enterprise systems in minutes with a managed Model Context Protocol (MCP) platform
hypothesis: Before we continue with the AI agent representation approach on this page, we should test if the CTR recovers with the previous version of the page or if the changed traffic (mix) caused the decline in CTR.
title: Logo rollback
evaluation: Revealing null result: after rolling back to the pre-grid version, the organic trial-intent CTR stayed at ~18% instead of returning to the pre-grid level of 24.5%. The earlier decline was therefore not (only) caused by the logo grid — a shift in the organic traffic mix is the more likely driver. Sample note: a short 7-day window on ~60 organic sessions/day with high day-to-day variation — directionally informative, but thin.
suggestions: Before the next /ai/ redesign, segment organic CTR by landing query/referrer to identify the mix shift. Watch the traffic-mix development on this page ahead of any new test.

original: H2: Connect your AI assistants and agents to hundreds of enterprise systems in minutes with a managed Model Context Protocol (MCP) platform
experiment:
- reduce them to the 5 most important: Claude (desktop), ChatGPT, Claude Code, Copilot, and Gemini
- move them below the fold but with a small teaser above
- add a Trial CTA below each of them (which shall link to the customized sign-up pages soon)
- link the logos themselves to the listed connectors or to a modal window with a prompt including an onboarding skill (Claude Code)
hypothesis:
As the CTR completely recovered after the rollback, we continue with the AI agent representation approach on this page.
By placing the AI agent logos less prominently, the distraction should be reduced.
Through additional Trial CTAs, the purpose of the AI agent logos should be clearer.
With additional AI sparkle icons attached to the AI agent logos, the additional functionality should be clearer.
title: Refined agent logos
evaluation: Positive and sustained: the refined presentation — five key agents below the fold, each with its own trial CTA — lifted the organic trial-intent CTR from 18.0% to 20.7% (+15%) in the evaluation window. The change remains live, and in the eight weeks since, the CTR has held at 21.7% (20.6% in the most recent week). The organic base stayed stable throughout (~46–61 sessions/day across baseline, window, and post-period), which strengthens confidence that this is a durable improvement, not a novelty or volume effect.
suggestions: Break the agent clicks down per agent (each cc_ai_*_trial event is tracked) and order the five logos by click share. Wire the per-agent CTAs to the planned customized sign-up pages.

original:
H2: CData Connect AI lets you plug any business application into any AI tool — like Salesforce into Anthropic Claude — for live, trusted answers and actions with zero data copies.
H3: Give Salesforce rich semantic context and real-time data from Anthropic Claude so it can answer precisely and take safe, effective actions across your business.
experiment:
- Spread the feature bullet points evenly across the entire width of the page in three columns.
- Change the order of the CTAs and make the Product Tour CTA transparent with a black border and black font color
hypothesis:
Since the features of Connect AI had the best CTR of the CTAs, we continue testing with this kind of information.
With a clearer presentation of these three bullet points, the hero is less text-heavy, and the CTAs are more in focus.
By changing the order of the CTAs and weakening the Product Tour CTA presentation, the CTR of the Trial CTA should increase.
title: CTA rearrangement
evaluation: Negative: this test restored the proven feature bullets and spread them across three columns while de-emphasizing the Product Tour CTA — yet the paid trial-intent CTR fell from 13.6% to 11.8% (−14%), and has averaged 9.2% in the six weeks after the window with the layout still live (8.5% in the most recent week). Since feature copy on its own had reached 15.0%, the layout and CTA-hierarchy changes plausibly cost around a fifth of the trial-intent CTR. Traffic note: window volumes were comparable (+11%), but the baseline period’s traffic was erratic (±50% daily swings while a non-converting Japanese paid wave receded) whereas the window itself was calm — and the joint-query visual (launched one day in) plus the top15 rollout overlap this pattern’s numbers.
suggestions: Unwind the layout/CTA-hierarchy changes toward the plain feature-bullet version, or re-run the CTA-hierarchy test in a clean window isolated from content changes. Keep layout tests and content/visual tests on non-overlapping schedules or disjoint page subsets.

hypothesis:
The CTR of the CTAs on /ai/integrations/[platform]/ is much better.
With a more meaningful visual presentation of what Connect AI can do with the Salesforce data source on /ai/connect/salesforce-to-claude, the willingness to start a trial should increase.
title: Joint-query visual
evaluation: Winner with a durable effect: the headline paid trial-intent CTR rose from 1.5% to 7.5% (+395%) in the evaluation window. However, the baseline’s traffic was extremely erratic (daily paid volumes swinging by multiples during a large non-converting Japanese traffic wave that peaked in the baseline and receded during the evaluation) — excluding that wave, the genuine effect is 7.0% → 12.4% (+77%). With the visual still live, the five weeks since average 11.1% on ~42 paid sessions/day — still clearly above the pre-visual level, though the most recent week reads 8.7%, so the sustained level is drifting toward the lower end of the window’s range and is worth re-checking in a few weeks.
suggestions: Extend the visual to organic-relevant pages beyond the paid set. Test variants: datasource-specific sample prompts, static vs. lightly animated, and placement above vs. beside the bullets.

title: Visuals for Top15
evaluation: Negative over nearly four weeks: the paid trial-intent CTR on the top15 pages runs at 8.8% vs. 12.5% in the weekday-aligned pre-period (−30%). The base remains thin — ~21 paid sessions/day across 15 pages, down from ~29 (−27%), which blurs the comparison — but the window’s length (46 clicks over 25 days, both halves below baseline at 8.3% and 9.2%) makes the direction hard to dismiss: the visuals have not reproduced the lift they delivered on the salesforce page. The change remains live.
suggestions: Break the effect down per datasource page — a few weak pages may drag the aggregate; keep the visual only where per-page numbers hold up. If the paid volume decline continues, re-check the SEM targeting for these 15 pages before attributing further CTR movement to the visual.

title: Changed CTA text
hypothesis: “Get Started Free” is more common and easier to grasp because it’s less confusing than the version with “...With Email.” The more common CTA text should increase the CTR.
evaluation: Strong positive, confirmed over the full 14-day window: renaming the main CTA from "Start Free With Email" to "Get Started Free" lifted the homepage's organic trial-intent CTR from 3.8% to 9.4% (+149%), with clicks more than doubling (63 → 146). The organic base was stable (~111 vs. ~120 sessions/day, −7%), and the lift held through both window weeks (9.9%, then 8.8%) — a durable wording effect, not a launch spike. The new CTA remains live; any post-window reading is confounded by the prefilled-deep-links experiment launched on the same page immediately afterwards.
suggestions: Roll "Get Started Free" out to the other Connect AI page types as its own experiment per pattern — the /ai/ hub and connect pages still use different wording. Judge the running prefilled-deep-links test against this window's 9.4% as the new homepage reference level. After that test, CTA prominence (placement, size, contrast) is the next homepage lever.

title: Prefilled deep links
original: The page provides onboarding prompts in modal windows for ChatGPT and Claude for copying & pasting.
experiment: Remove the modal windows in favour of deep links with prefilled prompts that paste them into ChatGPT and Claude automatically. Set a button for the listed CAI app in ChatGPT's and Claude's app directories right next to the button with the deep link with the prefilled prompts.
hypothesis: By removing modal windows and the additional step of copying & pasting the prompts, prompt usage should increase. This will be measured by tracking how clicks on the prompt buttons contribute to free trial clicks and to the overall free trial CTR.
evaluation: Neutral so far: replacing the copy-paste prompt modals with prefilled deep links leaves the homepage’s organic trial-intent CTR at 9.8% vs. 9.4% under the preceding period (+4% — within noise on a stable base of ~102 organic sessions/day). The prompt CTAs (tracked only since the experiment went live, so measured from zero) are used sparingly: 13 organic clicks — 0.85% of organic sessions, 29 clicks across all traffic — against 125 direct free-trial clicks, all of them via the Claude link; the ChatGPT prompt event has recorded no organic clicks yet. The first window half ran stronger than the second (11.3% → 8.6%); the test is still running, so the aggregate may settle either way.
suggestions: Verify the ChatGPT deep-link instrumentation — cc_ai_chatgpt_prompt exists but has not fired organically, which may be a wiring issue rather than non-usage. If prompt clicks stay this low relative to direct trial clicks, test making the prompt buttons more prominent or surfacing them to visitors arriving from AI-related searches.

title: Enriched datasource content
original: The page only included a hero and a section with to be connected AI agents or datasources (in case the page is about an AI agent).
experiment:
Copied all sections from the /drivers/[datasource]/mcp/ and the .../cloud/ page to the /ai/connect/[datasource]/ page.
- Natural language querying
- 3 Pillars (connect, context, control)
- Role-based query examples
- Compatible AI clients & agents
- 4 steps to go live
- BI/ETL tool integrations
- Get started free
hypothesis: With the enriched content on these pages, the SEO ranking should improve and the organic traffic increase. Due to the expanded information, the visitor could feel empowered to start a trial or choose an AI agent and start a trial from the corresponding X+Y page.
evaluation: The enriched pages turned this pattern from dormant into a working funnel entry: traffic went from effectively zero (~0–2 sessions/day) to ~272 paid and ~23 organic sessions/day, so no meaningful pre-period exists and this window sets the pattern’s reference level — a 10.4% paid trial-intent CTR (256 clicks in the first nine days). The organic growth from ~1 to ~23 sessions/day is an early positive signal on the SEO dimension of the hypothesis, though search effects need several more weeks to separate from the simultaneous traffic ramp-up. The path to the combination pages is being used: 74 clicks on the X+Y links so far (2.2% of paid sessions) — tracking for these links began with the experiment, so their adoption is measured from zero.
suggestions: Watch the organic-sessions trend weekly as the SEO signal — it needs 4–6 weeks to read cleanly. Compare the 10.4% paid CTR against the /drivers/ MCP pages the content came from, and test the X+Y links’ placement and prominence to grow the 2.2% path-to-combination rate.

title: Other SAP Technologies button
original: SAP related pages had no link to other SAP Technology pages.
experiment: "Other SAP Technologies" button for opening a modal window with 13 more SAP tools CAI can serve.
hypothesis: Providing an overview with all covered SAP tools increases his confidence in having found the right tool and his willingness to start a trial. This will be measured by the aggregated trial CTR and the usage of the "Other SAP Technologies" button.
evaluation: Too early for a verdict: three reliable days at ~11 paid sessions/day sit far inside noise range. Early signs of life only — the SAP pages collected 10 paid trial-intent clicks (a nominal 29.4% that means little at this base), and the new “Other SAP Technologies” button its first 4 clicks. The button’s usage tracking (cc_ai_sap_tools) started with its launch, so adoption is measured from zero.
suggestions: Judge after at least two full weeks — and at ~11 sessions/day, expect to need the full window plus post-window before the CTR is readable. If button usage stays low, test its label and placement; ordering the modal’s 13 tools by traffic is a cheap follow-up.

title: How-it-works
original: The X+Y pages show three feature columns above the fold. The “How it works” section contains a distracting MCP deep dive and a misleading 3-step guide.
experiment: Replaced the feature columns with a “How it works” section that includes a corrected 3-step guide and a link to the corresponding /kb/tech/[datasource]-cloud-claude/ page. The MCP deep dive remains at the bottom of the page.
hypothesis: Visitors to the X+Y pages are looking for “how,” not “whether.” The more prominent “How it works” section with the link to the corresponding /kb/ setup guide should increase the willingness to start a trial. The “How it works” marker, combined with the link to the /kb/ page, also makes it easier for AI agents to find a reliable answer to “how” questions, which should boost trials starting from AI agents.
